notes:
ACCESS: clean, no bot wall, no membership gate. probe.fetch() returned HTTP 200 throughout; roughly 90 requests were made across the session with probe.py's 2s/host pacing and not one 403 or 429. ROBOTS: https://www.simons.ca/robots.txt was fetched FIRST. It returns HTTP 200 with an EMPTY BODY - content-type text/plain, content-length 0, ETag "6a8eecfc-0", last-modified Wed 26 Aug 2026, served through Cloudflare. Verified as a genuine zero-byte file (r.content == b''), not a fetch failure: three separate fingerprints all returned 200/0 bytes, and https://www.simons.ca/en/robots.txt (a path that does NOT exist) returns the 164KB HTML soft-404 instead, which proves the root path is being served correctly. An empty robots.txt declares NO directives at all, so there is no Claude/ClaudeBot/anthropic-ai/Claude-Web group, no Disallow and no Crawl-delay. Nothing on this host is robots-disallowed. Per-host discipline (BATCH_BRIEF s1.3): the only other host in play was m.simons.ca, which appears in the mobile template's own product hrefs; I never REQUESTED m.simons.ca - I only parsed those hrefs out of the www response - and no m.simons.ca URL is recorded. The Bloomreach endpoints in the site's CSP (simons.bloomreach.co, *.dxpapi.com) were never contacted; they were unnecessary because the counts are server-rendered. TREE: taken from the site's OWN nav, three independent sources cross-checked. (1) The mega-menu, fetched as its own asset at https://www.simons.ca/en/menu_json.js - its Bathroom block lists the department https://www.simons.ca/en/bathroom--6823 plus only FOUR children (Bath Towels, Accessories & Wastebaskets, Shower Curtains & Hooks, Bath Rugs) and then a 'See more' link. THE MEGA-MENU TRUNCATES (BATCH_BRIEF s5). (2) The department landing page's own left-nav recovers TWO further children the menu hides: Baskets & Storage Items (--9822) and Body Care & Home Fragrances (--8989). (3) The category sitemap - /sitemap.xml -> /sitemap/www-ca/categorySitemap-en.xml, 8,287 category URLs - independently confirms the department has exactly these six children and two grandchildren (bath-towels/solid--8319, bath-towels/patterned--8112) and NOTHING else. The same sitemap was swept for bath|shower|toilet|soap|vanit|mirror|towel|sink|faucet|tap|tub|wc|bidet|hook|caddy|dispenser|wastebasket|hamper: the only non-Bathroom-department hits worth opening were /en/decor/mirrors--9830 and /en/fabrique-1840/decor/storage-hooks-shelves--9137 (both opened, both enumerated, both in review). There is NO sanitaryware, NO tap/faucet, NO bath/tub, NO toilet, NO shower enclosure and NO vanity unit anywhere in Simons' taxonomy - it is a department store's soft home offer, not a bathroom retailer. The /en/home-decor/new/bathroom/*, /en/home-decor/sale/bathroom/* and /en/vision/home/bathroom/* URLs in the sitemap are the SAME category ids with a new/sale/Vision filter applied - promotional facets, not categories (rules 25/28), and none is recorded. ROWS: two leaves. 'Accessories & Wastebaskets' (--6835, H1 'Bathroom Accessories') is Bathroom under rules 13/14/17 - all 175 distinct titles were read and they are soap dishes and pumps, toothbrush holders, tumblers, toilet brushes, toilet-paper holders and toilet-paper storage, towel racks and double towel racks, adhesive and wall hooks, wastebaskets and soft-close bins, bath trays, bath caddies, teak shower benches and footrests, tissue boxes, squeegees, drain hair catchers, shower mirrors and an LED lighted mirror. 'Baskets & Storage Items' (--9822, H1 'Bathroom Baskets & Storage') is Bathroom under rules 12 and 33 ('Bathroom > Bathroom Baskets = Bathroom') - the site's own hierarchy places it inside /en/bathroom/, and it carries genuine bathroom storage (corner and rectangular shower baskets, Bellwood freestanding over-the-toilet shelving, Fiji teak corner and wall shelving, bathtub trays, a Linear towel bar, teak towel hooks, a glass-door wall cabinet). DISCLOSED: it also carries jewellery boxes, decorative trays, coat racks and laundry baskets, i.e. general storage merchandised into the bathroom department - the hierarchy decides under rule 12 and the node is recorded whole, but the mixture is stated here rather than hidden. ROLL-UP CHECK (BATCH_BRIEF s5): the two recorded leaves are siblings, not a roll-up and its children. Product-id set intersection is 29 products - 29 of 175 and 29 of 156, i.e. neither contains the other and neither is a superset of any sibling. Both are therefore recorded. The 29 shared products are named in the enumeration dump (bath trays, shower baskets, adhesive hooks, teak shelving, decorative jars). The Bathroom department page itself was proved to hold no grid of its own, so no parent roll-up exists to withhold. QTY - SOURCE AND PROOF: the rendered figure in the PLP's own
N items. TWO TEMPLATES ARE SERVED: desktop fingerprints get a template with product tiles but NO counter, iOS fingerprints (safari17_2_ios / safari18_0_ios) get a template WITH the counter, data-current-page and data-total-pages. I used the iOS template for counts. PROOF, run on all eight Bathroom nodes and both review nodes outside the department - I paginated each node to its declared last page and summed the per-page product-card count (data-uid attributes), and the sum equalled the rendered figure EXACTLY on every single node with no exception: accessories 24+24+24+24+22+24+20+24+24+4=214; baskets 24+24+24+23+24+22+22+20=183; shower 24+21+6=51; bath-rugs 24+24+24+13=85; bath-towels 24+23+20+21+22+23+13=146; solid 24+24+24+17=89; patterned 24+15=39; body-care 24+24+24+23+24+23+22+20+19+10=213; decor/mirrors 24+24+23=71; fabrique storage 24+24+4=52. That is enumeration to exhaustion agreeing with the rendered total on ten nodes of widely differing size, which is the strongest verification available here. Pagination was verified to be REAL, not the IKEA trap: data-current-page increments with ?page=N and each page returns a different product set (page 2 of the accessories node shares no ids with page 1's first five). COLOURWAY DISCLOSURE (the Mango caveat): the counter counts CARD slots, and a product with two colourways can occupy two cards, so the distinct-product counts are lower - 175 for the 214 node, 156 for the 183 node, 37 for 51, 45 for 85, 41 for 146. The recorded qty is the site's own rendered listing figure per rule 26, with the distinct-product figure given here. Counts are stable: 214 and 183 were re-read on separate fetches with separate fingerprints and did not move. NO estimate, NO parent number reused, NO sibling sums. VERIFICATION: counts discriminate strongly (214/183/146/89/85/71/52/51/39). Every page's H1 was checked against the node requested and matched ('Bathroom Accessories', 'Bathroom Baskets & Storage', 'Bath Towels', 'Solid Bath Towels', 'Patterned Bath Towels', 'Bath Rugs', 'Shower Curtains & Hooks', 'Mirrors'). rel=canonical on every Bathroom node is self-referential (no alias to chase). No hreflang alternates are emitted. A first attempt to enumerate via the DESKTOP template was tried and REJECTED: it lazily hydrates and returned only 41 of 146 ids for Bath Towels, which would have produced a badly wrong figure - recorded here as a negative result so nobody repeats it. DEDUP (OPTION 1, URL-exact index): already_extracted() run on all 14 candidate/review/locale/host variants. ZERO hits. simons.ca appears in the index only via Furniture.xlsx with 15 records - 14 furniture nodes under /en/furniture/ plus /en/decor/poufs--8317 - and NONE of them is a bathroom node, a vanity or a bathroom cabinet, so OPTION 1 removes nothing here. Final.xlsx (the Home Decor / Lighting / Kitchen pass) does not cover simons.ca AT ALL, which is why /en/decor/mirrors--9830 is an index miss - it is genuinely unextracted, not a blind-spot artefact, and it is still kept out of rows on classification grounds, not dedup grounds. Blind spots worked explicitly: (a) canonicals - every recorded and reviewed node's rel=canonical was read and is self-referential; (b) LOCALE - Simons runs EN and FR off the SAME host with the same numeric category ids, so I pulled categorySitemap-fr.xml and index-checked all ten French twins (/fr/salle-de-bains--6823, /fr/salle-de-bains/accessoires-et-corbeilles--6835, /fr/salle-de-bains/paniers-et-articles-de-rangement--9822, /fr/salle-de-bains/rideaux-de-douche-et-crochets--6832, /fr/salle-de-bains/serviettes-de-bain--6824 and its /motifs--8112 and /unies--8319 children, /fr/salle-de-bains/tapis-de-bain--6829, /fr/salle-de-bains/soins-pour-le-corps-et-fragrances--8989, /fr/decor/miroirs--9830) - all miss, and Furniture.xlsx used the /en/ form, so the EN form is the right one to record; (c) cross-HOST alternates - the mobile host m.simons.ca was index-checked too (miss) and is not recorded; (d) one page two nav paths - the mega-menu path and the department left-nav path reach the same URLs, recorded once each. EXCLUDED and why: Bath Towels (+Solid, +Patterned), Bath Rugs and Shower Curtains & Hooks -> Textile (rules 15/16/20), all in review with qty and URL. Body Care & Home Fragrances -> not Bathroom, consumable personal care and fragrance (rules 3/21). Decor > Mirrors -> withheld as majority-decor with 6 medicine cabinets declared as residue (rule 29). Fabrique 1840 Storage/Hooks/Shelves -> withheld as general Decor/Storage with 2 toilet-paper holders declared. Inspiration by room > Bathroom -> shop-by-room re-cut, duplicate under rule 28. Bathroom department landing -> grouping row under rule 24, proved to have no grid of its own. No empty nodes were found: all eight Bathroom-tree URLs returned a populated grid. TWO KNOWN GAPS, stated rather than papered over: the four shower-hook sets inside the Textile-routed Shower Curtains & Hooks node, and the six medicine cabinets inside the Decor-routed Mirrors node, are real Bathroom products for which Simons publishes no Bathroom-only listing URL.

review.issue: ROUTED TO TEXTILE: bath towels, hand towels and bath sheets are Textile under rules 15/20. H1 'Bath Towels'. Rendered 146 items, PROVEN by enumeration to exhaustion (7 pages, per-page card counts 24+23+20+21+22+23+13 = 146 exactly). It has two children the Textile pass will want: Solid (H1 'Solid Bath Towels', 89 items, https://www.simons.ca/en/bathroom/bath-towels/solid--8319) and Patterned (H1 'Patterned Bath Towels', 39 items, https://www.simons.ca/en/bathroom/bath-towels/patterned--8112); both proved strict subsets of the parent by product-id set (18 of 18 and 21 of 21 contained). RULE 24 RESIDUE for the Textile pass: 89+39=128 of 146 cards, and 18+21=39 of 41 distinct product ids, so ~2 products / 18 cards sit in the parent under no child.

ROUTED TO TEXTILE: rule 16 - a textile bath mat is Textile. H1 'Bath Rugs'. Rendered 85, PROVEN by enumeration to exhaustion (4 pages, 24+24+24+13 = 85 exactly); 45 distinct products, every title enumerated. The assortment is chenille / boucle / memory-foam / cotton / Turkish-cotton bath mats. TWO NON-TEXTILE EXCEPTIONS were found and are flagged for the run owner rather than silently absorbed: 'Diatomite bath mat 39 x 60 cm' (diatomaceous-earth stone mat) and 'Bamboo slat bath mat 36 x 54 cm' - both would be Bathroom under rule 16's second clause, but they are 2 of 45 in a node whose primary product type is unambiguously textile, and the site gives them no separate node, so the whole node is routed to Textile. 6 of its products also appear inside the recorded Accessories & Wastebaskets leaf.

ROUTED TO TEXTILE (rule 20: shower curtains are Textile), WITH A DECLARED BATHROOM RESIDUE - rule 29 LOW CONFIDENCE, deliberately not forced into rows. H1 'Shower Curtains & Hooks'. Rendered 51, PROVEN by enumeration to exhaustion (3 pages, 24+21+6 = 51 exactly); all 37 distinct product titles were read. 33 of the 37 are shower curtains or shower liners (fabric, linen, waffle, PEVA, recycled polyester) = Textile. The remaining 4 are shower-hook SETS - 'Black double shower hooks Set of 12', 'Circular shower hooks Set of 12', 'Metallic beads double shower hooks Set of 12', 'Silver double shower hooks Set of 12' - which are Bathroom hardware under rules 6/17. The site offers NO child node and no separate hooks URL (verified against categorySitemap-en.xml: --6832 has no children), so there is no deepest valid Bathroom-only listing URL to record and rule 27 forbids inventing one. Recorded here in full so the 4 hook SKUs are not silently lost.

NOT RECORDED - inspected and rejected on primary product type (rule 2). Sixth child of the Bathroom department, H1 'Body Care & Home Fragrances' with a Fabrique 1840 banner. Rendered 213, PROVEN by enumeration to exhaustion (10 pages, 24+24+24+23+24+23+22+20+19+10 = 213 exactly), 180 distinct products. Contents are soaps, lotions, body and hand care, candles and home fragrance - consumable personal-care and fragrance goods. Rule 3's list of what counts as Bathroom covers furniture, fixtures, accessories, storage, ceramics and hardware; it does not cover body care, and rule 21 sends candles/fragrance to Decorative Home Accessories. Kept out of rows and out of the Bathroom count entirely. Flagged for whoever owns Beauty/Decor.

NOT RECORDED - rule 29 LOW CONFIDENCE with a declared Bathroom residue. Inspected specifically because rule 10 forbids skipping bathroom mirrors and rule 3 lists mirrored cabinets. H1 'Mirrors', under Home Decor > Decor, NOT under the Bathroom department. Rendered 71, PROVEN by enumeration to exhaustion (3 pages, 24+24+23 = 71 exactly); all 63 distinct titles read. 57 are general decorative wall / full-length / standing mirrors (arch, organic-shape, rattan-trim, teak, mango wood, brass) = Decor. 6 ARE MEDICINE CABINETS and would be Bathroom under rule 10 ('Cabinet Mirrors, Mirrored Cabinets'): 'Arched mirror medicine cabinet', 'Rounded mirror medicine cabinet' and four 'Black metal and mirror glass ... medicine cabinet' variants (curvy / rectangular / round / rounded corners). The node also holds a 'Rechargeable LED lighted mirror' and a 'Black standing double-sided mirror', but those two are also stocked inside the recorded Accessories & Wastebaskets Bathroom leaf, so they are already captured there. Simons publishes NO medicine-cabinet or bathroom-mirror node (categorySitemap-en.xml shows --9830 has no children), so recording this node would import 57 decor mirrors into Bathroom and recording nothing loses 6 medicine cabinets - the honest resolution is review, not a guess. Index-checked: miss (Final.xlsx never covered simons.ca at all).

NOT RECORDED - general Decor/Storage under rules 30-33, checked because rule 17 puts robe/bathroom hooks and bathroom shelves in Bathroom. H1 'Storage, Hooks & Shelves at Fabrique 1840', sits in the Fabrique 1840 marketplace zone under Decor, not under Bathroom. Rendered 52, PROVEN by enumeration to exhaustion (3 pages, 24+24+4 = 52 exactly), 38 distinct products. 36 are wall shelves, coat racks, shoe racks, laptop/computer stands, trays, magazine and letter holders, bookends and a log stand = general Decor/Storage. Only 2 are Bathroom under rule 14 - 'Minimalist toilet paper holder' and 'Steel toilet paper holder' - which is not enough to reclassify the node, and the site gives them no bathroom-scoped URL. Declared here so the two are not silently skipped.

NOT RECORDED - SHOP-BY-ROOM RE-CUT, a duplicate under rule 28 (BATCH_BRIEF s5: shop-by-room re-cuts are duplicates, not extra rows). Editorial room page reached from the mega-menu's 'Inspiration by room' column; carries no H1 and mixes items already counted elsewhere - page 1 alone drew from Bath Towels, Bath Rugs, Shower Curtains & Hooks, Accessories & Wastebaskets, Baskets & Storage Items, Body Care AND Decor > Mirrors (a medicine cabinet), plus one clothing item ('Brown teddy bear leopard plush headband') that proves it is a merchandising cut and not a taxonomy node. Rendered 108. Recording it alongside the two real leaves would double-count.

NOT RECORDED as a leaf - rule 24: it is the parent of six real children and is therefore the grouping row. Confirmed to carry NO product grid of its own: fetched on both desktop and iOS templates, zero product tiles, zero data-uid entries, no 'N items' counter, H1 is the editorial 'Elegant Bathroom Decor Essentials'. So there is no rule 24 residue at department level - every product sits in a child.
